({{langx|ca-valencia|Elx Club de Futbol, S.A.D.}}) is a Spanish professional [[association football club|football]] club based in [[Elche]], [[Province of Alicante]], in the [[Valencian Community]], Spain. Founded in 1923, the club competes in [[La Liga]], holding home matches at the [[Estadio Martínez Valero]], with a capacity of 33,732 seats.{{cite web |url=http://www.elchecf.es/club/estadio-martinez-valero |title=ESTADIO MARTÍNEZ VALERO {{!}} Elche |website=www.elchecf.es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222234615/http://www.elchecf.es/club/estadio-martinez-valero |archive-date=2015-12-22}} Founded in 1923 as the result of a merger between all of the town's clubs, Elche entered the league system in 1929, reaching [[Segunda División]] in [[1934–35 Segunda División|1934]] and [[La Liga]] in [[1958–59 Segunda División|1959]], finishing fifth in the latter tournament in [[1963–64 La Liga|1963–64]]. The club were runners-up in the [[Copa del Rey]] in [[1969 Copa del Generalísimo|1969]]. ==History== ===Foundation and early years=== Elche Club de Fútbol was founded in the winter of 1923, after the [[Mergers and acquisitions|merger]] of all of the town's football teams. The club's first-ever game was against [[Monóvar]], where they beat the home team 4–0, and its first official match was a 2–0 win over [[Crevillente Deportivo|Crevillente]]. In its first years Elche, like many teams of the time, played in an all white uniform.{{Cite web|url=https://www.elchecf.es/club/hitos-historicos|title=La historia del Club {{!}} Elche - Web Oficial|website=La historia del Club {{!}} Elche - Web Oficial|language=es|access-date=2019-10-19|archive-date=December 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191212234627/https://www.elchecf.es/club/hitos-historicos|url-status=live}} The team played its first league season in 1929–30, in the [[Tercera División]], achieving promotion to the [[Segunda División]] in 1934. However, Elche suffered relegation for the first time six years later, but were promoted back the following season. In the late 1950s, Elche achieved two consecutive promotions from the third level to [[La Liga]], securing the club's first promotion to the latter competition with a 3–0 success against [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]] in 1959. ===1959–78: La Liga=== [[File:Panórámica del Estadio Martínez Valero.jpg|thumb|323x323px|[[Estadio Martínez Valero]]]] Elche opened [[1959–60 La Liga|its first season in the top level]] with a 1–1 draw against [[Real Oviedo]], the first goal being scored by [[Vicente Pahuet]]. The club finished tenth out of 16 sides, nine points ahead of relegated [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] – the campaign included a 2–1 comeback home victory over [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], but also a 2–11 loss at [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]]. [[1960–61 La Liga|The following season]] saw the team having to compete in the [[Promotion and relegation|relegation/promotion]] play-off, where it overcame a 0–1 loss in the away leg against Atlético Ceuta with a 4–0 home victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist5969.html|title=Spain, Final Tables 1959–1969|access-date=February 4, 2023|archive-date=March 31, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331190632/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist5969.html|url-status=live}} Elche achieved their best-ever league finish in [[1963–64 La Liga|1963–64]], ranking in fifth position. The season also saw the club's [[reserve team]], [[Elche CF Ilicitano|Elche Ilicitano]], promote to [[Segunda División]].[https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist5969.html Spain 1963/64] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331190632/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist5969.html |date=March 31, 2023 }}; at RSSSF In [[1969 Copa del Generalísimo|1969]] the club reached their first and only [[Copa del Rey]] final, following victories over [[Pontevedra CF|Pontevedra]], [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] and [[Real Sociedad]]. The semi-final against the latter was won 2–0 in a replay in neutral [[Madrid]], as the tie had finished 4–4 on aggregate; the final, played on 15 June at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]] in the same city, brought a 0–1 loss to [[Athletic Bilbao]].[https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancup1969.html Spain – Cup 1969] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407002729/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancup1969.html |date=April 7, 2023 }}; at RSSSF After twelve seasons Elche were relegated to division two in [[1970–71 La Liga|1971]], having finished second from bottom.[https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist6979.html Spain 1970/71] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230210034605/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist6979.html |date=February 10, 2023 }}; at RSSSF [[1972–73 Segunda División|Two years later the team returned to the main category, as champions]]. Its second spell in the top flight lasted five seasons, often immerse in relegation fights as the best campaign ([[1974–75 La Liga|1974–75]]) ended with the club in eighth position; at the end of [[1977–78 La Liga|1977–78]] the side returned to the second division after finishing 17th out of 18 clubs, the last game being a 4–4 draw with [[Atlético Madrid]], which was led 2–4 with five minutes remaining.[https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist6979.html Spain 1977/78] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230210034605/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist6979.html |date=February 10, 2023 }}; at RSSSF ===80s and 90s: severe financial crisis=== [[File:Elche Club de Fútbol league performance 1929-present.svg|thumb|Chart of Elche CF league performance 1929–present]] After the relegation Elche suffered in 1978, they never managed to gain promotion to the top flight – in fact, in the first five years since their return to the second level, they were fourth on three occasions and fifth on two (and on a further two, even on points with the third-placed team but with a worse goal difference), often losing the chance of promotion on the last matchday. Especially traumatic was the finish of the [[1980–81 La Liga|1980–81 season]]: with one game remaining, they were second two points ahead of [[Rayo Vallecano]] and [[Racing de Santander]], only needing a draw against [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] at the ''[[Estadio Martínez Valero|Martínez Valero]]''; the game ended however in a loss, and Elche finished with 45 points alongside [[CD Castellón|Castellón]], Cádiz, Racing and Rayo. A promotion finally occurred at the end of [[1983–84 Segunda División|1983–84]], even though Elche only finished fifth in the [[Season (sports)#Regular season|regular season]] – the first two positions were occupied by [[Real Madrid Castilla]] and [[Athletic Bilbao B]], who could not promote as reserve sides. The whole of the [[1984–85 La Liga|top division campaign]] was spent in the relegation zone, and relegation consequently befell as 17th. In [[1987–88 Segunda División|1988]] they were promoted again for another cameo appearance, as the side went on to finish dead last with eighteen points, dropping down a category alongside [[Real Murcia]], who they trailed by nine points; the last match for years in the category was a 1–3 away loss against [[Real Zaragoza]], the goal coming courtesy of [[Alfonso Fernandez (footballer)|Alfonso Fernández]]. After the relegation in 1989, Elche started to suffer heavily in the financial department, and were relegated to [[Segunda División B]] – the new third level created in 1977 – at the end of [[1990–91 Segunda División|1990–91]]. During the better part of the 1990s the club reached the second division promotion playoffs, only to consecutively fall short. In the 2016–17 season, Elche were relegated to the third division after 18 years in the professional league. One year later, Elche was promoted back to the second division after defeating [[Villarreal CF B|Villarreal B]] in the final play-off promotion. It managed to spend two seasons in the second division, when the main squad was in the top flight. == Rivalries == Elche CF and [[Hércules CF]] have been fierce rivals for a long time. Their rivalry, known as the Derbi de la provincia de Alicante, began way back in the 1925/26 season when Elche CF joined the official regional league.  Since then, these teams have clashed over a hundred times.{{Cite web |title=HISTORIA {{!}} Hércules - Elche: 92 años de derbis |url=https://www.elchecf.es/noticias/historia-hercules-elche-92-anos-de-derbis |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.elchecf.es |language=es}} The rivalry between Elche CF and [[Real Murcia CF]] is a historical one. Their first official match was during the 1928–29 season. Their frequent meetings, known as the Derbi del Sureste (Southeast Derby), make this fixture the most played in the history of the [[La Liga2|Segunda División]].{{Cite web |last=Redacción |title=Historia de los Elche-Real Murcia |url=https://www.goldelmurcia.es/noticia/historia-de-los-elche-real-murcia/2977-historia-de-los-elche-real-murcia |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.goldelmurcia.es |language=es-es}} Another of the most notable rivalries is with [[Levante UD]]. These teams have a long history of intense regional competition across various divisions, including [[LaLiga|Primera]], [[La Liga2|Segunda]], and [[Segunda División B|Segunda B]], creating a fierce atmosphere both on the pitch and in the stands.{{Cite web |title=Elche - Levante, vuelve una rivalidad histórica {{!}} Deporte Valenciano |url=https://www.deportevalenciano.com/2014/04/23/elche-levante-vuelve-una-rivalidad-hist%C3%B3rica |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=Deportevalenciano |language=es}} Elche CF's rivalries with [[Hércules CF|Hércules]] and [[Real Murcia CF|Real Murcia]] stem from regional proximity, while their rivalry with [[Levante UD|Levante]] developed over numerous competitive clashes.
